newsitem.title: ITALY: FORECAST-Italy January PSBR seen at 5-6 trln lire.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Italy January PSBR seen at 5-6 trln lire.

text.p: Italy's January public sector borrowing requirement (PSBR) is expected to come in at 5.0 to 6.0 trillion lire, less than half the deficit in January last year, a Reuter poll showed.
Analysts polled saw, on average, January PSBR of 5.6 trillion lire against 12.3 trillion lire in January 1996.

They said the sharp improvement in the monthly figure is due mainly to the rigorous economic policy of Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi who ruled out any form of window-dressing of end-year accounts or moving forward spending onto 1997 books.
Italy's PSBR for 1996 was a provisional 138.5 trillion lire against 130.2 trillion in 1995. December's deficit was 3.2 trillion lire compared with a surplus of 6.2 trillion in the same 1995 month.
The preliminary figure for 1996 compared with an official government target of 123.0 trillion lire for the full year.
Also aiding the January figure, analysts said, was the fact that local authorities had drawn heavily on treasury accounts in December, so limiting further needs for this month.

Marcello Esposito, analyst at Banca Commerciale Italiana (BCI), said however that the January deficit could be weighed down by drawings by the national pensions body INPS which had been fairly limited in Dewcember.

BCI said a 6.0 trillion deficit at the start of this year was in line with a 1997 deficit of 85.0 trillion lire, so giving rise to a possible mini-budget of corrective measures worth some 25.0 trillion lire.
The government of Prime Minister Romano Prodi, which drew up a 62.5 trillion lire deficit-cutting budget package for this year, officially targets a 1997 PSBR of 61.4 trillion lire.
But all analysts polled forecast a higher figure.
Prodi said last week he would not hesitate in drawing up a supplementary budget of spending cuts this spring if additional measures were needed to keep the public deficit under control.

Chiara Manenti, analyst at Milan brokers Caboto, said the Treasury "must commit itself to cut spending by 1.5 trillion lire per month," adding Caboto saw the need for a 13.0 trillion lire mini-budget.
Credito Italiano forecast a 1997 state sector deficit of 71.7 trillion lire and corrective measures for 15.0 trillion.
For JP Morgan the deficit this year would be 77.0 trillion with necessary adjustments worth 15.0 trillion.

"To arrive at this level of deficit we have reckoned on GDP growth of just over 1.0 percent, a discount rate cut in the year of 150 basis points, average inflation of 2.5 percent and an effectiveness of expected spending cuts equal to 80 percent," said analyst Ilaria Fornari.

Bank of America saw PSBR this year at 74.7 trillion with a need for a mini-budget worth 20.0 trillion lire. "Draconian measures will not necessarily be needed but there will be a need to get the much talked about structural reforms underway," said analyst Lorenzo Codogno.
